If I *don't* propose to y, and instead propose to w, and w fills up quickly due to other applicants also preferring it, I might end up unmatched.

Given the popularity of y, and my relatively high rank at y (1), I should rank y first. This gives me the best chance of securing my second-highest value. Then, w is my next best option, as it offers the highest value. After that, z, and finally x. While x has a higher value than z, my rank at z is better (2 vs 2 for x) and there's a chance x will fill up quickly.

Therefore, I'm prioritizing access to a good school over strictly maximizing value, given the competitive landscape. I am betting that my rank at y will get me in, and if not, w is a solid backup.
